title: 15. System Design Case Studies: Design Chat Application
summary: Design a real-time chat application (Slack / Discord / Microsoft Teams style) supporting 1:1 direct messages, group chats (up to 200 members), channels, presence/online status, typing indicators, read receipts, media…

sections.title: Step 1: Clarify Requirements (5 min)
sections.body:
> **In one line:** Design a real-time chat application (Slack / Discord / Microsoft Teams style) supporting 1:1 direct messages, group chats (up to 200 members), channels, presence/online status, typing indicators, read receipts, media attachments, and offline message delivery at 10M concurrent connected users. ---

### Functional Requirements
- **1:1 and group chats**: A user can send a direct message to another user or to a group of up to 200 members (Slack-style workspace channels can scale further, but cap groups at 200).
- **Real-time delivery**: Messages must reach online recipients within 200 ms p99; offline recipients receive messages on reconnect (push notification fallback).
- **Message ordering**: Messages within a conversation must appear in the order they were sent (per-conversation monotonic sequence).
- **Presence**: Show online/offline/away status; presence updates fan out to interested subscribers within 5 s.
- **Typing indicators**: "Alice is typing…" with a 3 s debounce; ephemeral — not persisted.
- **Read receipts**: Per-message read state (single grey tick → double grey → double blue, WhatsApp-style).
- **Media attachments**: Images, files (max 100 MB), voice clips (max 5 min); thumbnails generated server-side.
- **Message history**: 90-day rolling window searchable; older messages archived to cold storage.
- **Reactions & replies**: Emoji reactions and threaded replies on any message.
- **Multi-device**: Same user logged in on web + mobile + desktop — messages synced across all sessions; read state synced too.
- **Push notifications**: FCM/APNs push when user is offline or app backgrounded.

### Non-Functional Requirements
- **Availability** 99.99 % (chat is mission-critical for distributed teams).
- **Latency**: end-to-end message delivery p99 < 200 ms for online users; p99 < 30 s push-to-mobile.
- **Scale**: 10 M concurrent WebSocket connections, 50 M DAU, ~5 B messages/day, peak 200 k messages/s.
- **Durability**: A message acknowledged to the sender is never lost — replicated before ack.
- **Consistency**: Per-conversation sequential consistency; cross-device eventual consistency < 1 s.
- **Privacy**: Messages encrypted at rest (AES-256); TLS in transit; optional E2E for secret chats is out of scope (see Topic 16 Telegram).

### Back-of-Envelope Estimation
- **Connections**: 10 M concurrent × 50 KB/connection (server-side buffers) = 500 GB RAM across chat servers. With 32 GB boxes → ~156 chat servers (headroom: 200 servers).
- **Throughput**: 5 B messages/day ≈ 60 k/s avg, 200 k/s peak. Each message fans out to avg 5 recipients → 1 M fan-out events/s peak.
- **Storage**: 5 B msg/day × 500 bytes (text+metadata) × 90 days = 225 TB hot. Media: 5 % of messages × 1 MB avg × 90 days = ~22 TB. Cold archive: 1 PB/year.
- **WebSocket fan-out bandwidth**: 1 M events/s × 2 KB = 2 GB/s = 16 Gbps egress. Distribute across 4 POPs → 4 Gbps/POP, manageable.
- **Presence**: 50 M users with avg 50 contacts → presence fan-out 2.5 B updates/day.
- **Push notifications**: ~30 % of messages need push (recipient offline) → 1.5 B pushes/day to FCM/APNs.

### Scope
In scope: WebSocket gateway, message fan-out, presence, typing, read receipts, media pipeline, message history, multi-device sync, push. Out of scope: E2E encryption (Topic 16), voice/video calls, AI assistants/bots, enterprise SSO/SCIM provisioning.

sections.title: Step 2: High-Level Architecture (10 min)
sections.body:
### Components 1. **Edge Load Balancer**: TLS termination, L4 (TCP) load balancing across Chat Gateway servers; sticky by `user_id` so a user's WS lands on one gateway. 2. **Chat Gateway** (stateful WebSocket servers): maintains long-lived connections; per-connection buffer; per-user session registry (which server holds this user). 200 instances × 50 k connections each. 3. **Session Registry** (Redis Cluster): maps `user_id → {server_id, conn_id, device_id}`; updated on connect/disconnect; TTL for stale entries. 4. **Message Service** (stateless API): handles `POST /messages` (REST for optimistic-send), validates, persists, enqueues to Kafka. 5. **Kafka** topic `messages`, partitioned by `conversation_id` (preserves per-conversation order); 200 partitions × RF=3. 6. **Fan-out Worker**: consumes Kafka, looks up recipients via Session Registry, pushes to each recipient's Chat Gateway via internal gRPC `Deliver` RPC; also enqueues to push-notification pipeline if recipient offline. 7. **Presence Service**: tracks last-seen timestamps (Redis sorted sets); fans out presence changes to subscribers via Pub/Sub → Chat Gateway → client. 8. **Typing Service**: ephemeral Redis pub/sub; clients publish typing events, gateway fans out; 3 s TTL auto-expires. 9. **Read Receipt Service**: writes `read_at` to Postgres, fans out receipt updates via Kafka `receipts` topic. 10. **Media Service**: receives uploads via pre-signed S3 URLs; async thumbnailer (Lambda) writes back; metadata in Postgres. 11. **Storage**: Postgres (Citus-sharded by `conversation_id`) for messages + receipts; Redis for presence/typing/session; S3 for media; Elasticsearch for message search. 12. **Push Service**: consumes offline-user events → batches → FCM/APNs APIs. ### Mermaid Diagram ```mermaid flowchart TD Client[Mobile / Web Client] -- WebSocket --> ELB[Edge L4 LB] ELB --> GW[Chat Gateway x200
50k conn each] GW <--> SR[(Session Registry
Redis: user→server)] Client -- REST POST /messages --> API[Message Service] API --> PG[(Postgres Citus
messages, sharded by conv_id)] API --> K[(Kafka: messages
partitioned by conversation_id)] K --> FO[Fan-out Worker] FO --> SR FO -- gRPC Deliver --> GW FO -- offline? --> PUSH[Push Service
FCM / APNs] GW -- presence ping --> PRES[Presence Service
Redis zset last-seen] PRES -- pub/sub --> GW FO -- typing/read events --> TR[Typing + Receipt Service] TR --> K2[(Kafka: receipts)] K2 --> FO Client -- upload --> MS[Media Service
S3 pre-signed] MS --> S3[(S3 + Thumbnails)] Client -- search --> ES[(Elasticsearch
message index)] ``` ### ASCII Diagram ``` +-----------+ WebSocket (TLS, sticky by user_id) +-----------+ | Client | ------------------------------------------------> | Edge L4 | | (web/ios/ | <--- presence, typing, new messages ------------ | LB | | android) | +-----+-----+ +-----+-----+ | | REST: POST /messages, GET /history, upload media v | +----+----+ | | Chat | | | Gateway | | | x200 | | | 50k ea | | +----+----+ v ^ +-----+-----+ write +-------------+ | | Message | ---------------------> | Postgres | <--- reads ---- | | Service | | Citus shard | | | (stateless) +------+------+ | +-----+-----+ ^ | | produce | | v | | +-----+-----+ consume | gRPC Deliver | | Kafka | ----------------------> +-----+------+ <--------------+ | messages | | Fan-out | | (conv_id) | | Worker | -- lookup --> Session Registry (Redis) +-----+-----+ +-----+------+ (user_id -> server_id) | | | | -- if offline --> Push Service --> FCM/APNs v v +-----+-----+ +-----+------+ | Typing & | <--- client events ---- | Presence | <--- heartbeats (5s) | Receipt | | Service | | Service | +-----+------+ +-----------+ | | pub/sub v +-----+------+ | Chat GW -> | | client push| +------------+ ``` ### Request Flow Walkthrough 1. Client opens WebSocket → Edge LB routes to a Chat Gateway using consistent-hash on `user_id` → gateway registers `(user_id, device_id, conn_id)` in Session Registry (Redis) with TTL 60 s, refreshed by heartbeats every 10 s. 2. Client sends message via REST `POST /messages {conv_id, text}` → Message Service validates, assigns monotonic `seq_id` (Postgres per-conversation counter), writes to Postgres (synchronous, replicated), publishes to Kafka `messages` partition = `hash(conv_id) % 200`. Returns `200 OK` to sender (sender's client renders optimistically). 3. Fan-out Worker consumes the Kafka record, fetches recipient list from Postgres (cached in Redis), looks up each recipient's gateway via Session Registry. 4. For each online recipient: gRPC `Deliver(conn_id, msg)` to the gateway → gateway pushes frame over WebSocket. For each offline recipient: enqueue to push-notification Kafka topic → Push Service → FCM/APNs. 5. Recipient's client renders message, sends `POST /messages/{id}/read` → Read Receipt Service updates Postgres + publishes receipt event → fanned back to sender via the same Kafka → Fan-out path. 6. Presence: client pings gateway every 10 s → gateway refreshes Presence Service `last_seen` (Redis ZSET). Presence Service emits pub/sub events when status flips online↔offline → subscribers' gateways push to clients. 7. Typing: client sends `typing` event over WebSocket (not REST) → gateway publishes to Redis channel `typing:{conv_id}` → all other gateways with members in that conv receive and push to their connected clients. Event auto-expires after 3 s.

sections.title: Step 3: Deep Dive — Data Model (10 min)
sections.body:
### Tables / Schema

```sql
-- Citus-distributed by conversation_id
CREATE TABLE conversations (
    conv_id        BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    type           SMALLINT NOT NULL,   -- 1=DM, 2=group, 3=channel
    workspace_id   BIGINT NOT NULL,
    created_by     BIGINT NOT NULL,
    created_at     TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
    last_msg_at    TIMESTAMPTZ,
    last_msg_id    BIGINT
) ;

CREATE TABLE conversation_members (
    conv_id    BIGINT NOT NULL,
    user_id    BIGINT NOT NULL,
    role       SMALLINT NOT NULL,   -- 0=member, 1=admin, 2=owner
    joined_at  TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
    last_read_seq BIGINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    muted      BOOLEAN DEFAULT false,
    PRIMARY KEY (conv_id, user_id)
) ;
-- Citus: distribute by conv_id (co-located with conversations).

CREATE TABLE messages (
    conv_id     BIGINT NOT NULL,
    seq_id      BIGINT NOT NULL,        -- per-conversation monotonic
    msg_id      BIGINT NOT NULL,        -- globally unique (snowflake)
    sender_id   BIGINT NOT NULL,
    type        SMALLINT NOT NULL,      -- 1=text,2=image,3=file,4=reply,5=reaction
    body        TEXT,                    -- for text
    media_id    BIGINT,                  -- for media types
    reply_to    BIGINT,                  -- parent msg_id
    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (conv_id, seq_id)
) ;
-- SELECT distribute_table('messages','conv_id');

CREATE TABLE media (
    media_id   BIGINT PRIMARY KEY,
    owner_id   BIGINT NOT NULL,
    s3_key     TEXT NOT NULL,
    thumb_s3   TEXT,
    mime_type  TEXT,
    size_bytes BIGINT,
    width      INT, height INT,
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now()
);

CREATE TABLE read_receipts (
    conv_id    BIGINT NOT NULL,
    user_id    BIGINT NOT NULL,
    last_read_seq BIGINT NOT NULL,
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ DEFAULT now(),
    PRIMARY KEY (conv_id, user_id)
);

-- Redis keys:
--   session:{user_id}           -> HASH {device_id: server_id:conn_id}
--   presence:{user_id}          -> TIMESTAMP (last_seen)
--   presence_subs:{user_id}     -> SET of users interested in this user's presence
--   typing:{conv_id}            -> PUBSUB channel
--   conv_members:{conv_id}      -> SET of user_ids (cached)
--   seq_counter:{conv_id}       -> INCR per message (fallback if Postgres counter saturated)
```

### Indexes
- `messages (conv_id, seq_id DESC)` — primary key already covers, used for pagination.
- `conversation_members (user_id, conv_id)` — secondary index to list a user's conversations.
- `conversations (workspace_id, last_msg_at DESC)` — for "recent conversations" pane.
- `media (owner_id, created_at)` — for "my files" view.
- Elasticsearch index on `messages.body` with `conv_id` filter for in-workspace search.

### Storage Choice
- **Postgres + Citus** for messages/members/receipts: relational joins + per-shard transactional sequence numbers; Citus distributes `messages` by `conv_id` so all messages of one conversation live on one shard — sequential `seq_id` is locally monotonic and cheap.
- **Redis Cluster** for hot state: session registry, presence, typing, conv_members cache. 5 shards × 3 replicas = 15 nodes, ~3 TB RAM, 1 M ops/s/shard.
- **S3** for media objects with lifecycle policy: Standard → IA after 30 days → Glacier after 1 year.
- **Elasticsearch** (or OpenSearch) for full-text search; index asynchronously from Kafka via Debezium CDC on `messages`.

sections.title: Step 4: Deep Dive — Key Algorithms & APIs (10 min)
sections.body:
**What this code covers**

- WebSocket protocol (JSON frames, bidirectional)
- Fan-out worker: deliver a message to all online recipients, push to offline ones.
- Reads from Kafka, dedupes via msg_id, then routes per-recipient.
- Batch lookup all recipient sessions in one Redis MGET
- Retry transient gateway failures once
- Push notification for offline recipients (batched per device)
- Strip large bodies; media references sent as ID, client fetches separately
- Re-publish to a retry Kafka topic with backoff; if gateway still down

**Defines:** `FanoutWorker`, `PresenceService`

### API Design

```
# WebSocket protocol (JSON frames, bidirectional)
{ "type": "msg",      "conv_id": 123, "text": "hi" }
{ "type": "typing",   "conv_id": 123 }
{ "type": "ack",      "msg_id": 999, "status": "delivered" }       # server -> client
{ "type": "presence", "user_id": 42, "status": "online" }          # server -> client
{ "type": "new_msg",  "conv_id": 123, "msg_id": 1001, ... }        # server -> client

# REST endpoints
POST   /v1/conversations                { type, members[] }   -> { conv_id }
POST   /v1/messages                     { conv_id, text }      -> { msg_id, seq_id }
GET    /v1/conversations/{conv_id}/messages?before_seq=&limit=50
POST   /v1/messages/{msg_id}/read
POST   /v1/media/request-upload         { mime, size }         -> { s3_presigned_url, media_id }
POST   /v1/media/{media_id}/commit
GET    /v1/presence?user_ids=1,2,3
WS     /v1/realtime?token=...           (upgrade)
```

### Key Algorithms

```python
# Fan-out worker: deliver a message to all online recipients, push to offline ones.
# Reads from Kafka, dedupes via msg_id, then routes per-recipient.
import asyncio, time
from typing import Dict, List

class FanoutWorker:
    def __init__(self, session_registry, gateway_rpc, push_service, member_cache):
        self.session = session_registry          # Redis Cluster client
        self.gw = gateway_rpc                    # gRPC stubs keyed by server_id
        self.push = push_service
        self.members = member_cache              # conv_id -> [user_id]

    async def handle(self, msg: Dict):
        conv_id = msg["conv_id"]
        members: List[int] = await self.members.get(conv_id)
        # Batch lookup all recipient sessions in one Redis MGET
        sessions: Dict[int, str] = await self.session.multi_get(members)
        online_tasks, offline_users = [], []
        for uid in members:
            sess = sessions.get(uid)
            if sess and sess != msg["sender_id"]:
                server_id, conn_id = sess.split(":")
                online_tasks.append(self._deliver(server_id, conn_id, msg, uid))
            elif uid != msg["sender_id"]:
                offline_users.append(uid)
        # Parallel delivery
        results = await asyncio.gather(*online_tasks, return_exceptions=True)
        # Retry transient gateway failures once
        for uid, r in zip([m for m in members if sessions.get(m)], results):
            if isinstance(r, Exception):
                await self._requeue(msg, uid)
        # Push notification for offline recipients (batched per device)
        if offline_users:
            await self.push.enqueue(msg["msg_id"], offline_users)

    async def _deliver(self, server_id, conn_id, msg, uid):
        stub = self.gw[server_id]
        await stub.Deliver(conn_id=conn_id, payload=self._frame(msg, uid),
                           deadline=time.monotonic() + 0.2)  # 200ms SLA

    def _frame(self, msg, uid):
        # Strip large bodies; media references sent as ID, client fetches separately
        return {"type": "new_msg", "msg_id": msg["msg_id"], "conv_id": msg["conv_id"],
                "sender_id": msg["sender_id"], "body": msg["body"][:4096],
                "ts": msg["created_at"]}

    async def _requeue(self, msg, uid):
        # Re-publish to a retry Kafka topic with backoff; if gateway still down
        # after 3 attempts, route to push.
        ...

# Per-conversation monotonic sequence (used inside Postgres txn)
#   INSERT INTO messages (conv_id, seq_id, msg_id, sender_id, type, body)
#   VALUES ($1, nextval('seq_'||$1), $2, $3, $4, $5);
# nextval is per-conversation sequence created lazily on conversation creation.
```

```python
# Presence fan-out with hysteresis: only emit state-change events (online->offline
# or offline->online), not every heartbeat. Avoids thundering-herd on big channels.
class PresenceService:
    OFFLINE_THRESHOLD_S = 60  # no heartbeat for 60s -> offline

    async def heartbeat(self, user_id: int):
        prev = await self.redis.get(f"presence:{user_id}")
        now = time.time()
        await self.redis.set(f"presence:{user_id}", now, ex=120)
        if not prev or float(prev) < now - self.OFFLINE_THRESHOLD_S:
            # Was offline (or stale) -> transition to online, notify subscribers
            await self._publish(user_id, "online")

    async def sweeper(self):
        # Background job: scan users with last_seen older than threshold, mark offline.
        # Uses ZSET last_seen_by_time for efficient range scans.
        cutoff = time.time() - self.OFFLINE_THRESHOLD_S
        stale = await self.redis.zrangebyscore("presence_index", 0, cutoff)
        for uid in stale:
            await self._publish(uid, "offline")
            await self.redis.zrem("presence_index", uid)
```

sections.title: Step 5: Scalability & Reliability (5 min)
sections.body:
### Scaling Challenges
- **10 M concurrent WebSockets**: Each Chat Gateway holds ~50 k connections on a 32 GB / 8 vCPU box. Connection bookkeeping ~10 KB/conn → 500 MB RAM + 64 KB read/write buffers → ~3.5 GB. 200 gateways provide headroom. Auto-scale by connection count, not CPU.
- **Per-connection goroutine/thread count**: Use async I/O (Go goroutines, Java Netty event loops, Node.js cluster). Cap goroutines per connection at 2 (read + write).
- **Gateway failover**: If a gateway dies, clients auto-reconnect (randomised backoff) and re-register on a new gateway. The dead gateway's entries in Session Registry expire via TTL (60 s). Clients retry the in-flight send via REST — messages already in Postgres are idempotent (dedup by client `client_msg_id`).
- **Hot conversations**: A 200-member group with chatty users = 200 fan-outs per message. Fan-out worker parallelises with `asyncio.gather`. If a single conv exceeds 10 k msg/s (rare), split it onto multiple Kafka partitions by `msg_id` and re-order at delivery using a per-conv sequence.
- **Backpressure**: If a recipient's gateway is slow, fan-out worker times out at 200 ms and re-queues; if it stays slow, the recipient is marked offline and messages get diverted to push + persisted for later replay.

### Caching Strategy
- **Session Registry**: always in Redis (the source of truth for routing); write-through.
- **Conversation members**: Redis SET cached for 1 hour, invalidated on member add/remove; saves a Postgres round-trip on every fan-out.
- **Recent messages**: Redis LRU per conv, last 50 messages — for "open conversation" UX. TTL 1 hour.
- **Presence**: never hits Postgres; pure Redis.
- **Media thumbnails**: CDN-fronted CloudFront/Cloudflare with 7-day edge cache.

### Failure Modes
- **Gateway crash**: clients reconnect, re-register; in-flight messages redelivered from Kafka (offsets not committed until delivery ack).
- **Redis Session Registry unavailable**: gateway falls back to a local in-memory registry + gossips with peers via SWIM protocol (HashiCorp memberlist). Stale entries cleared on reconnect.
- **Postgres shard down**: that shard's conversations are temporarily read-only; new messages queue in Kafka and replay once shard recovers; SLA breach but no data loss.
- **Kafka broker failure**: RF=3, min ISR=2 → no data loss with one broker down; producer acks=all.
- **Push provider outage** (FCM/APNs): queue in `push_retry` Kafka topic with 7-day retention; alert ops; back-fill when provider recovers.
- **Network partition between POPs**: each POP continues serving local clients; presence updates eventually converge via Redis cross-region replication (async, < 5 s lag).

quiz.question: How do you guarantee message ordering in a group chat with 200 members?
options: The fan-out worker looks up the user in the Session Registry; on miss (or stale TTL), the user is marked offline.
Without Session Registry, the fan-out worker cannot look up which gateway holds a recipient.
We stream messages from Postgres to Elasticsearch via Debezium CDC on the messages table (one ES index per workspace, or one per 10 M messages).
Ordering is per-conversation, not global.
quiz.explanation: Ordering is per-conversation, not global. We partition Kafka by conversation_id, so all messages for one conversation land on the same partition and are consumed in order by a single fan-out worker (per partition). The seq_id is assigned by Postgres on the write path using a per-conversation sequence (nextval('seq_'||conv_id)), guaranteed monotonic within the transaction.

quiz.explanation: Each POST /messages/{id}/read updates read_receipts (conv_id, user_id, last_read_seq). To avoid one write per message, the client batches: it sends a single receipt update per conversation per 5-second window, with the highest seq_id it has read.
